newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SEOUL STOCKS SEEN RISING DESPITE PROFIT-TAKING.
newsitem.headline: SEOUL STOCKS SEEN RISING DESPITE PROFIT-TAKING.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to continue advancing on Tuesday despite some profit-taking, brokers said.
"Profit-taking is likely to set in today following three consecutive days of rises," said Chung Chang-shik of Dongsuh Securities. "But the upward momentum would be maintained."
The recent appreciation of the Japanese yen against the dollar, which has improved sentiment on expectations of rising exports, would remain an important factor, brokers said.
The composite stock index closed Monday up 4.23 points to 765.07.
Brokers said institutional interest on core blue chip counters would continue in anticipation of an economic turnaround.
Insurance shares, which outperformed the market on Monday, were also forecast to stay strong, they said.
The sector was boosted by a local report of a rise in applications for travel insurance following the Korean Air crash in Guam last week.
Brokers said any news involving the cash-strapped Kia Group would be closely monitored.
